items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: Now, Johnny Dots was a pretty good clarinet player.

ctx.x: He wouldn't get Gut Bucket, though? Huh?

Well, yeah, what you call Gut Bucket, you understand? It was the tune. The Gut Bucket is the tune you play. It ain't the man, it's the tune, it's the piece you're playing that makes it Gut Bucket, you see? Of course, some guys play Gut Bucket because they can't play otherwise, you see? Now, Johnny Dots was a pretty good clarinet player. In his style, you know, he played well, you see? Now, you might call him Gut Bucket, you see? But a man like Teo, you couldn't call him Gut Bucket because he's a scholar, you…

items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: Baby Dots and Johnny Dots and all of them, they come right from Louisiana.

ctx.x: Huh? You remember the Sam Morgan band? Oh yeah, sure. He was way under me, you understand.

I was playing a long time before they were coming. All the fellas come to little country towns around, you know, like over and the fellas, they come right up the river there, you know. And they come here and start playing. Baby Dots and Johnny Dots and all of them, they come right from Louisiana. And the Kid Punch. Yeah, he's from here too, right up the country there.
Did he have any distinctive style of playing?
